definitions.explanation: The act of handing something over from one party to another. Used for physical objects, documents, property, or responsibilities.

examples.japanese: {鍵|かぎ}の{受|う}け{渡|わた}しは{明日|あした}です。
{荷物|にもつ}の{受|う}け{渡|わた}しは{玄関|げんかん}で{行|おこな}います。
examples.english: Package delivery will take place at the entrance.

examples.japanese: {物件|ぶっけん}の{受|う}け{渡|わた}し{日|び}が{決|き}まったら、{連絡|れんらく}してください。
examples.english: Please contact us once the property handover date is decided.

notes:
Compound noun formed from {受|う}ける ('to receive') and {渡|わた}す ('to hand over'). Describes the transaction of passing something from one party to another, emphasizing both the giving and receiving sides of the exchange.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鍵|かぎ}の{受|う}け{渡|わた}し: key handover
- {荷物|にもつ}の{受|う}け{渡|わた}し: package delivery
- {受|う}け{渡|わた}し{日|び}: delivery date, handover date
- {受|う}け{渡|わた}し{場所|ばしょ}: handover location
- {業務|ぎょうむ}の{受|う}け{渡|わた}し: work handover (when changing positions)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {引|ひ}き{渡|わた}し: delivery, surrender — often used in legal and real estate contexts; implies formal transfer of possession
- {納品|のうひん}: delivery of goods — specifically for commercial deliveries
- {引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ: taking over, succession — focuses on continuing responsibilities rather than physical transfer
